result.target_topic: Impairment Recognition for AFS Securities Intent to Sell
result.target_summary: If management intends to sell an AFS security or it is more likely than not they will be required to sell before recovery of the amortized cost basis, the entire unrealized loss is recognized in Other revenues and the amortized cost basis is written down to fair value. Any previously established allowance for credit losses (ACL) is written off in this scenario.

Since D069 is already matched to D062, and D070 is matched to D064, D063 stands as a single-sided current disclosure representing the intent-to-sell accounting which was bundled with the general policy in D069. It is a supported split.

comparisons.peer_topic: Impairment and credit loss evaluation for AFS debt securities
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation evaluates Available-for-Sale (AFS) debt securities below amortized cost for impairment or expected credit losses (ECL); if intent to sell exists, it is written down to fair value through earnings. For held securities, qualitative parameters and discounted cash flow analyses determine if unrealized losses stem from ECL, with recognized losses adjusted via valuation allowance, while market-related declines go to OCI.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and BAC apply an identical primary criterion for AFS securities: if management intends to sell or it is more likely than not they will be required to sell before recovery, the entire unrealized loss is recognized in earnings. MS specifies that any previously established ACL is written off in this scenario (ms_2024_8_P086_S002), while BAC describes the outcome as writing the security down to fair value through earnings without explicitly detailing the ACL write-off in the same sentence, though both address the intent-to-sell trigger (bac_2024_8_P048_S002).

sentences.text: If so, the amortized cost basis is written down to the fair value of the security such that the entire unrealized loss is recognized in Other revenues, and any previously established ACL is written off.
If the Corporation intends to sell or believes it is more likely than not that it will be required to sell the debt security, it is written down to fair value through earnings.

comparisons.peer_topic: AFS State and Municipal Bonds Impairment Recognition Policy
comparisons.peer_summary: Full impairment is recognized in earnings for AFS bonds where Citi plans to sell or is more-likely-than-not required to sell prior to recovery. For bonds not intended for sale, an allowance for expected credit losses is recorded, capped at the difference between amortized cost and fair value.
comparisons.comparison: Citi (C) and MS share the same intent-to-sell impairment recognition policy: if Citi plans to sell or is more-likely-than-not required to sell prior to recovery, full impairment is recognized in earnings, mirroring MS's recognition of the entire unrealized loss (c_2024_8_P422_S001 vs ms_2024_8_P086_S002). However, C explicitly details the treatment for securities NOT intended for sale, noting that an allowance for expected credit losses is recorded and capped at the difference between amortized cost and fair value (c_2024_8_P422_S002), whereas MS's provided text focuses primarily on the intent-to-sell write-down mechanics without elaborating on the non-sale impairment methodology in the cited sentences.

sentences.text: If so, the amortized cost basis is written down to the fair value of the security such that the entire unrealized loss is recognized in Other revenues, and any previously established ACL is written off.

For AFS state and municipal bonds with unrealized losses that Citi plans to sell or would more-likely-than-not be required to sell prior to recovery of value, the full impairment is recognized in earnings.

For AFS state and municipal bonds where Citi has no intent to sell and it is not more-likely-than-not that the Company will be required to sell, Citi records an allowance for expected credit losses for the amount it expects not to collect, capped at the difference between the bond's amortized cost basis and fair value.

comparisons.peer_summary: Available-for-sale securities are accounted for at fair value with unrealized gains and losses included in accumulated other comprehensive income, while realized gains use the specific identification method. Impairment is recognized if the firm intends to sell or is likely required to sell before recovery, but no such losses or credit loss provisions were recorded in 2024 or 2023.
comparisons.comparison: While GS and MS both account for AFS securities at fair value with unrealized gains/losses in OCI, GS's cited disclosure does not explicitly describe the intent-to-sell impairment trigger or the resulting earnings recognition mechanics that are central to MS's policy (ms_2024_8_P086_S001-S002). GS's text focuses on general accounting treatment and hedging relationships (gs_2024_8_P276_S001) and quantitative OCI gains (gs_2024_8_P280_S001) rather than the specific impairment recognition criteria regarding intent to sell.

sentences.text: AFS securities in an unrealized loss position are first evaluated to determine whether there is an intent to sell or it is more likely than not the Firm will be required to sell before recovery of the amortized cost basis.

If so, the amortized cost basis is written down to the fair value of the security such that the entire unrealized loss is recognized in Other revenues, and any previously established ACL is written off.

Available-for-sale securities are accounted for at fair value, and the related unrealized fair value gains and losses are included in accumulated other comprehensive income/(loss) unless designated in a fair value hedging relationship.

comparisons.peer_summary: Available-for-sale (AFS) debt securities are considered impaired if fair value is below amortized cost. Impairment losses are recognized in earnings if the firm intends to sell the security or it is more likely than not that the firm will be required to sell it before recovery, measured as the full difference between amortized cost and fair value.
comparisons.comparison: JPM and MS follow the same impairment recognition logic for AFS securities: if the firm intends to sell or is more likely than not required to sell before recovery, the full difference between amortized cost and fair value is recognized as an impairment loss in earnings (jpm_2024_8_P399_S001-S002). MS uses similar language regarding intent and the write-down of the amortized cost basis to fair value with the entire unrealized loss recognized in Other revenues (ms_2024_8_P086_S001-S002). Both policies trigger on the same 'intent to sell' or 'likely required to sell' threshold.

sentences.text: AFS securities in an unrealized loss position are first evaluated to determine whether there is an intent to sell or it is more likely than not the Firm will be required to sell before recovery of the amortized cost basis.

If so, the amortized cost basis is written down to the fair value of the security such that the entire unrealized loss is recognized in Other revenues, and any previously established ACL is written off.

The Firm recognizes impairment losses in earnings if the Firm has the intent to sell the debt security, or if it is more likely than not that the Firm will be required to sell the debt security before recovery of its amortized cost.

In these circumstances the impairment loss is recognized in investment securities gains/(losses) in the Consolidated Statements of Income and is equal to the full difference between the amortized cost (net of allowance if applicable) and the fair value of the security.
